classification.difficultyReason: Find the common pole height using one cable, then use inverse sine to determine the angle of the other cable.

content.prompt: A flagpole is stabilised by two cables affixed to the top of the pole. The first of these makes a $40^\circ$ angle to the ground and is 4.9 metres long. The second cable is 3.8 metres long. Determine the angle $\theta$ that the second cable makes with the ground, to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Two cables meet at the top of a vertical pole, with ground anchors on opposite sides. The pole foot has a right-angle mark. The decorative flag is omitted; all mathematical lines and labels are retained without shading.
spec.mathematics: Left cable length 4.9 m and ground angle 40 degrees; right cable length 3.8 m and unknown acute ground angle theta; common perpendicular height x. Drawing coordinates are derived from the supplied lengths and angle and are not printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels are visible.

answer.short:
$\theta\approx55.98^\circ$.

Find the common pole height using sine, then use inverse sine for the second cable.
